title: Final Destination
tagline: Death's got a list. Dessert's on it.
about: A student's vision gets him and a handful of classmates off their flight to Paris, but death has a plan, and they're all on it.
cue: Serve the croque monsieur bites when the class boards Flight 180 for Paris.
faces: Mount Abraham High, Senior Class Trip to Paris
Seatbelts on and tray tables down for the meal service. Nobody swaps seats, and nobody trades their dessert either.
Gin, lemon and sugar syrup shaken cold and topped with sparkling wine, with a lemon twist.
Paris class trip croque monsieur bites
Toasted ham and gruyère sandwiches with mustard and béchamel under a golden cheese top.
Slow-caramelised onions folded through sour cream and cream cheese with chives, with salted crisps.
Rocky Mountain High on the speakers. Sit tight.
Chicken thighs braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions, with crusty baguette.
The other choice on the dinner trolley.
Little lemon and honey sponge cakes baked in shell moulds.
Meals subject to availability. Trolley prices in local currency. Alex's vision in the departure lounge. Mr Bludworth at the funeral home. Card 180/2000. Images: TMDB.

    StartersParis class trip croque monsieur bitesToasted ham and gruyère sandwiches with mustard and béchamel under a golden cheese top, cut into squaresHow to make it30g butter2 tbsp plain flour250ml milk1/4 tsp ground nutmeg1/4 tsp salt8 slices of white sandwich bread2 tsp dijon mustard150g sliced ham150g gruyère, gratedMelt the butter, stir in the flour, whisk in the milk and simmer to a thick béchamel. Season with the nutmeg and salt.Heat the grill. Spread 4 slices of bread with mustard, top with the ham and half the gruyère and close the sandwiches.Toast in a dry frying pan until golden on both sides.Spread the béchamel over the tops, scatter with the rest of the gruyère and grill until bubbling.Cut each into 4 squares.Window seat French onion dipSlow-caramelised onions folded through sour cream and cream cheese with chives, with salted crispsHow to make it3 brown onions, thinly sliced30g butter1 tbsp olive oil1/2 tsp salt250g sour cream125g cream cheese, soft1 bunch chives, snipped1/4 tsp black pepper200g plain salted crispsCook the onions in the butter and oil with the salt over low heat, stirring often, until deep golden and jammy.Cool.Beat the sour cream and cream cheese until smooth and fold in the onions, most of the chives and the pepper.Chill so the flavours settle.Scatter with the rest of the chives and serve with the crisps.Honey roasted peanutsRocky Mountain High on the speakers. Sit tight.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsFlight 180 coq au vinChicken thighs braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions, with crusty baguetteHow to make it8 chicken thigh cutlets, skin on1 tsp salt1/2 tsp black pepper1 tbsp olive oil150g bacon, diced12 small pickling onions, peeled250g button mushrooms2 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp plain flour1 tbsp tomato paste500ml red wine250ml chicken stock4 thyme sprigs2 bay leaves2 tbsp parsley, chopped1 baguetteSeason the chicken with the salt and pepper and brown skin side down in the oil in a wide heavy pan, then turn, brown and lift out.Fry the bacon, onions and mushrooms in the same pan until golden, then add the garlic.Stir in the flour and tomato paste, pour in 500ml red wine and 250ml chicken stock, and add the thyme and bay.Return the chicken skin side up, cover and simmer gently.Uncover and simmer until the sauce coats a spoon.Scatter with parsley and serve with torn baguette.Volée Airlines salmon en papilloteThe other choice on the dinner trolley, for the passengers who stayed on Flight 180How to make it4 salmon fillets1 fennel bulb1 zucchini2 lemons1 dill40g butter300g long grain rice1 parsleyHeat the oven to 200°C. Slice the fennel, zucchini and 1 lemon thinly.Lay each salmon fillet on a sheet of baking paper on a bed of fennel and zucchini, top with lemon, dill and butter, season and fold into a tight parcel.Bake on a tray for 15 minutes.Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, rest for 5, then stir through chopped parsley and the juice of the other lemon.Open the parcels at the table and serve with the rice.SweetsBludworth's funeral parlour madeleinesLittle lemon and honey sponge cakes baked in shell moulds, dusted with icing sugarHow to make it2 eggs100g caster sugar1 tbsp honey1 lemon, zested100g plain flour1 tsp baking powder110g butter, melted and cooled2 tbsp icing sugarWhisk the eggs, caster sugar, honey and lemon zest until pale and thick.Fold in the flour and baking powder, then 100g of the melted butter.Cover and chill the batter.Heat the oven to 200°C and brush a madeleine tray with the rest of the butter.Spoon in the batter and bake until domed and golden.Turn out, dust with icing sugar and serve warm.DrinksPremonition French 75Gin, lemon and sugar syrup shaken cold and topped with sparkling wine, with a lemon twistHow to make it120ml gin2 lemons, juiced60ml sugar syrup500ml sparkling wine, chilled1 cup ice1 lemon, peeled into twistsShake the gin, lemon juice and sugar syrup hard with the ice.Strain into 4 chilled flutes.Top with the sparkling wine and add a lemon twist.
